title: Rate-aware fragmented batcher with KV windowing for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response length traffic (short prompts with long generated responses and vice versa) causes our continuous batching scheduler to either over-coalesce (increasing p95 latency for short tail requests) or to produce many small batches that fragment KV memory slabs and underutilize GPUs.

Goal: Implement a rate-aware fragmented batcher that uses a sliding KV windowing heuristic and length-gating to keep tail latency within SLO while improving overall token throughput and reducing GPU memory fragmentation. The feature should be optional and toggleable per-route.

Design summary:
- Add a rate estimator that tracks per-route request arrival rates and per-length histogram (buckets: 0-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048).
- Fragmented coalescing: instead of a single continuous coalescer, we maintain 2 active coalescing lanes per GPU slab: a short-lane optimized for low-latency short requests and a long-lane that allows larger accumulation for long-response generation.
- KV windowing: KV allocations are assigned soft-windows (time-based) and are eligible for prefetch/compact when underutilized for X ms. Windows are tuned by rate-estimator to avoid frequent reallocations that cause slab fragmentation.
- Length-gating: When a long-response request arrives, it can be gated to the long-lane if the estimated time-to-complete for current short-lane accumulation would violate the short-lane latency SLO.
- Headroom estimator: A lightweight GPU memory headroom predictor prevents overcommit and triggers proactive KV eviction at configurable watermarks (default 0.78).

Why different from existing approaches: avoids monolithic continuous coalescing; uses arrival-rate signal + explicit lanes to reduce latency p95 for short dialogs while improving GPU token throughput for long generations. It focuses on reducing KV slab churn via time-windowed KV compaction rather than purely eviction-by-age or size thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route toggle implemented and documented in runtime config
p95 latency for short requests (<32 tokens prompt) improves or stays within 10% of baseline SLO under mixed load scenarios
Token throughput increases by >= 8% in 60/40 long/short synthetic mix compared to continuous v1
GPU memory fragmentation (measured as free-slab-churn metric) reduced by >= 25% vs continuous baseline
No increase in OOM incidents in stress tests (0 OOMs on 1000-run gen suite)
End-to-end e2e tests and canary rollout gating in console (traffic switch) configured
notes: Initial microbench harness built in runtime/bench/fragmented-batcher. See local run logs at /var/log/bench/frag-batcher-2026-02-25.txt
We chose 2 lanes after ablation: 1 lane gives poor long-gen throughput; 3 lanes increased scheduling overhead with marginal gains.
KV window default: 120ms idle -> eligible for compaction. Tuned after experiments (see comments).
Headroom watermark default 0.78 (empirical) but exposed as route-level config for Dedicated customers.
This ticket intentionally avoids changing long-term KV eviction policy; it layers windowing and compact hints to existing slab allocator.
